item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukraine has launched a drone strike that killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant and attacked a missile-fuel plant in St Petersburg, while Russia has continued missile and drone attacks on Ukrainian power facilities and the Northern Bridge. Russia has begun rationing petrol after Ukrainian strikes damaged its second-largest refinery in Saratov, prompting Rosneft to cap sales, and a Russian FPV drone wounded three energy workers in Sumy Oblast. Leaked data indicate that more than 400,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war. Trilateral peace talks involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine are now underway in Abu Dhabi, and UCDP recorded 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024.

item.title: Israel and Hezbollah: the situation
item.description:
Israel has built a 90km road network and opened new bases in southern Lebanon while continuing cross-border incursions, including an Israeli man who entered Lebanon and was returned by UN forces. Israeli airstrikes have hit Qantara and renewed shelling across southern Lebanon, wounding a Lebanese footballer and prompting the detention of a 65‑year-old retired engineer. Hezbollah persists in firing artillery at Israeli positions and has begun cash payments to war victims and displaced families. French investigators are probing alleged Israeli war crimes, and protests against Israeli attacks have occurred in Sweden. The conflict caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
The United States recently struck Iran's Qeshm Island and disabled a commercial vessel attempting to run a blockade in the Gulf of Oman, while Iran launched a missile that hit a building in Tel Aviv. Iran continues to use the Strait of Hormuz as leverage in the regional confrontation. The United States has offered a $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear program, and France warned of a response to a cyberattack on supermarkets blamed on Iran. The conflict has already caused 123 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Yemen and the Red Sea: the situation
item.description:
Houthi forces continue a month-long siege of Taiz while Yemeni government troops have seized the al-Jawf mountain range, intensifying front-line fighting. Houthi rockets damaged the Saudi Aramco tower in Riyadh and the coalition intercepted a cruise missile, a long-range anti-tank guided missile and downed a ballistic missile aimed at Medina. A Saudi strike near Sanaa killed 22 civilians, mostly women and children, and a Houthi-claimed airstrike near the capital also killed 22 people. The vital East-West pipeline was hit, prompting Saudi officials to inspect Aramco facilities, and Saudi Arabia shot down missiles fired at Riyadh after a Houthi attack on the pipeline. The conflict caused 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Syria: the situation
item.description:
Syria has begun dispatching troops to Saudi Arabia to fight the Houthis, while denying any deployment inside Yemen. Saudi-led forces and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis have escalated attacks, including a strike that damaged the Saudi Aramco Tower in Riyadh. In Damascus countryside, heavy clashes erupted around Wadi Barada between Syrian forces and unidentified opponents. Jordan and Syria have signed eleven cooperation agreements covering economic projects, security coordination and a rail link, deepening bilateral ties. The conflict caused 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
Iran-linked drones struck the Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan, halting production and cutting about 2.8 GW of power, while Iraqi forces responded with airstrikes on three suspected militants and a tunnel in Kirkuk's Zghaitun Valley. Iraqi officials identified the launch site of the Khor Mor attack and accused militia groups, whose leaders are seeking Chinese and Russian air defenses. Baghdad reopened the Sheeb border crossing with Iran after a three-week closure and agreed to withdraw Turkish forces from the Zilkan base by the end of 2026. 396 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The Sudanese army has secured Bakori and Sali, repelled attacks in the Blue Nile and advanced in West Kordofan, while the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have carried out drone strikes that killed civilians in Blue Nile and White Nile states and caused a two-week power blackout that raised prices. A senior RSF commander has defected to the Sudanese army after 13 years, and Pakistan has signed a 1.5 billion-dollar security cooperation deal with Sudan. Drones now account for two thirds of child casualties, and Darfur faces looming famine as crop failures worsen humanitarian access. 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Ugandan truck drivers were ambushed and killed, with their bodies released by South Sudanese authorities. The Mayom County commissioner and his family were assassinated, and a soldier and a civilian were killed in an attack in Kapoeta North. Communal fighting in Tonj East left 11 dead before calm returned, and churches reported worship disruptions due to violence. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

Somali Danab commandos launched security operations in Middle Shabelle targeting Al-Shabaab extortion networks. US forces carried out overnight airstrikes against ISIS positions in Puntland, Somalia. Burkina Faso, after aligning with Russia, has partnered with another Western state on its 36th reunification anniversary. item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:

Kidnappings persist, with children and families abducted in Kaduna, Sokoto and other areas, and police have rescued a six-year-old boy in Kaduna. ISIS-linked militants killed 33 people, prompting the Africa CDC to call for a humanitarian corridor to protect Ebola response.
